segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakashwani. I am Saira Muchthapa with the news at 9.
The headlines
Government clears defence procurement for armed forces worth 2,12,000 crore rupees,
82% of acquisitions to be sourced from Indian industry.
Cyclone urnabbed intensifies over Bay of Bengal.
Centre reviews preparedness as Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, Telangana,
Chhattisgarh and Puducherry brace for impact.
Relief scheme for exporters offering 95% risk cover for shipments extended till 31st of March
amid West Asia crisis.
Usage of 100% ethanol fuel allowed in flex fuel vehicles as government amends motor vehicles
rules.
And Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla inaugurates two-day BRICS parliamentary forum meeting in
New Delhi.
And now the news in detail.
The Defence Acquisition Council, D.A.C., chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has cleared
several capital acquisition proposals for the armed forces worth approximately Rs. 2,12,000.
The Defence Ministry has said nearly 82% of the procurements will be made from the Indian
industry. For the Indian Army, approval has been granted for the procurement of several
systems, including high-mobility vehicles, self-propelled tracked gun systems, light multi-role
helicopters, very short-range air defense systems, surveillance UAVs, integrated surveillance
and strike systems, and long-range kamikaze drone systems. More from our correspondent.
The high-mobility vehicles, which will be procured for Indian Army, will enhance
operational capabilities, logistic support, and mobility in challenging terrains. The
The self-propelled tracked-gun system will provide matching mobility and firepower to
mechanized formations.
The light multi-role helicopters will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air
Force for surveillance, combat search and rescue of troops, humanitarian assistance,
and disaster relief, among others.
For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of active-of-world decoy
system and other major naval platforms.
This will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles' defense, especially against
modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries.
For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of helicopters, air defence
systems, weapons and mobile X-band Doppler weather radar system to enhance the air defence
and war-fighting capabilities.
Anand Kumar, Akash Mani, New Delhi.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has stressed the need to develop cutting-edge technologies
and strengthen supply chains to reduce import dependence and achieve technological
superiority in the second phase of self-reliance in the defence sector.
Mr Singh was speaking at the 5th edition of the Naval Innovation and
Integernization Seminar, Swaavillamban, 2026 in New Delhi today.
In this phase of self-reliance, we must not only manufacture products in our own country,
but also ensure that the production is cost-effective, operationally superior and globally
competitive. So, the question is not just about quantity, it is also about quality,
security, efficiency, and affordability.
We should also consider whether we can prepare a priority list for the development of technologies
and products that are required for both civilian and military shipping.
Cyclonics Tom Arnab continues to intensify over the Bay of Bengal as it moves towards
the Andhra Desh coast, raising concerns over adverse weather in various parts of the
country.
The evolving weather system is likely to bring heavy rainfall in Andhra
Pradesh, Telangana, Southern Orissa, Puducherry, South and Central
Chhattisgarh, apart from eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
The Intermetrological Department has said, the storm is likely to
intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over West-Central Bay of
Bengal tonight.
It is very likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm over
the same region tomorrow, before crossing the Andhra
Coast on Wednesday.
Andhra Desh, Chief Minister and Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparedness measures to tackle
the evolving situation, a report.
Chief Minister and Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to continuously monitor the cyclones
movement and take all necessary precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property.
District collectors have been instructed to alert people in vulnerable coastal areas
and shift them to cyclone shelters wherever necessary.
The Indian Metrological Department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall
with wind speeds likely to reach 115 to 125 km per hour and gets up to 140 km per hour
during landfall. The state disaster management authority has urged people to remain vigilant
and follow official advisories. Meanwhile, educational institutions in seven districts
have been declared closed on October 27th and 28th as a precautionary measure.
Arsa Igrish, for Akashwari News, Vijay Bada
The Odisha government has intensified its preparedness by deploying ministers and
rescue teams to coordinate response efforts. Our correspondent has the details.
Cyclonic storm Arnab is moving westwards over the Bay of Bengal about 550 km southeast of
Gopalpur in the latest available reports. In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati, Rai Gada, Kuraput
and Malkangiri are under a red warning for Wednesday. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi
centres in the five districts will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday. Railways
have cancelled eight trains and cut till two services. Ajay Prakashan, Chief Minister
Mohan Charanamaji has assigned eight ministers to oversee preparedness in vulnerable districts,
while 302 rescue teams have been kept ready.
Rekhaas Das for Akashvani News, Bhuvaneswar.
Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the Bay of Bengal along an off-the-coast
of Andhra Desh, Chorissa and Yarnam in Puducherry until Thursday.
Meanwhile, Cabinet Secretary Dr. T. B. Somanathan today chaired a meeting of the National
Crisis Management Committee to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in the Bay
of Bengal.
call. The chief secretaries and senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh
and Puducherry, apprised the committee of the preparatory measures being undertaken by
the state governments and local administration. Dr. Somanathan stressed the need to ensure
zero loss of life, minimize damage to property and infrastructure, and restore essential
services at the earliest. The Rajasthan government has declared
that 80 thessals across 14 districts as drought affected due to deficient rainfall and damage
to Kharif crops. Our correspondent has the details.
The state government has issued notifications in this regard, taking into account deficient
rainfall and damage to Kharif crops. 69 thessals have been classified as severely
affected while 11 have been categorized as moderate affected. The declaration will remain
in effect for the next six months. The government's decision will facilitate the opening of order
depots for livestock in the affected areas. Recovery of agricultural loans will also remain
suspended for six months.
Jitendra Divedi, Aakashwani News, Jaipur
Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel has declared four districts – Kach, Jamnagar,
Portpandar and Devubhumi Dwarka as drought affected due to low and delayed rainfall.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Welcome back, you're listening to Evening News.
The Centre has extended the timelines of the Resilience and Logistics Intervention
for export facilitation or relief scheme until the 31st of March next year in view of
ongoing geopolitical disruptions in West Asia. The initiative aims to encourage exporters to obtain
export-credited guarantee cooperation of India cover for upcoming shipments to specified regions
by providing 95% risk coverage. The government has allowed the use of E-100 ethanol fuel in
vehicles specifically designed to run on flexible fuel under amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles
rules 1989. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways issued a Gazette notification
in this regard. The decision will pave the path for original equipment manufacturers to
launch vehicles engineered to run 100% bioethanol fuel.
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sita Raman today said the Reserve Bank of India was taking
measures to prevent sudden fluctuations in the value of the rupee. Speaking to reporters
at Tiruchirapalli in Tamil Nadu, Ms. Seetha Raman said that India's fiscal deficit has
been declining year after year, with the government working towards reducing the debt-to-GDP ratio
to 50 per cent by 2030.
Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnav today flagged off the Jaipur-Khati-Purta-Tata Nagar-Shantra-Galchi
Express train.
Mr. Vaishnav participated in the program through video conferencing.
Speaking on the occasion, the minister said, the new train service connecting
Jaipur with Jamshedpur and Kolkata will improve rail connectivity between Rajasthan, Uttar
Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal.
Today the new train is being launched for Jamshedpur and Kolkata. There has been a strong demand
from Purvanchal, Jharkhand and Bengal for travelling to Jaipur. This will be fulfilled
very conveniently. Thousands of Rajasthani migrant brothers and sisters, business people,
students and everyone else who wants to come to Jaipur will benefit greatly from this facility.
Union Food and Consumer Affairs Minister Prahla Joshi today reviewed the availability of essential
commodities. He held a discussion with the Secretary and senior officials of the Department
of Consumer Affairs in New Delhi on the prevailing price situation, festive season
market trends and stock requirements for the coming year. In a social media post, Mr
Joshi noted, that adequate buffer stalks of essential commodities are in place, with prices
showing signs of stabilization.
Union Minister and senior BJP leader Rajnath Singh has criticized Congress President Malik
Arjun Khare over his alleged remarks on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late father. Talking
to media, Mr Singh said the Congress has suffered not just a political downfall but
also an ideological decline. Delhi BJP today held a protest near the residence of Congress
his president over his alleged remarks.
You are listening to news at 9 on Akash Maneen.
Welcome back.
Lok Samha speaker Om Birla today inaugurated the 12th BRICS parliamentary forum at the
historic Samvidhan-Sadan in Parliament House complex in New Delhi today.
day. The discussions during the two-day meeting is likely to focus on resilience, innovation,
cooperation and sustainability, covering AI oversight, emerging technologies and sustainable
development. Speaking on the occasion, the Lok Sabha speaker said,
Parliament can play an important role in strengthening mutual understanding and trust,
reducing international tensions and finding peaceful solutions to global challenges.
challenges. Mr. Birla highlighted key challenges including regional conflicts, wars, economic
instability, trade tensions, terrorism and climate change.
The true strength of parliamentary diplomacy lies in our ability to incorporate a democratic
perspective into international relations, while respecting each other's sovereignty
and to translate mutual understanding, trust and dialogue fostered through shared experiences
and collective actions into concrete cooperation.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi also attended the inaugural session and met the leaders
of the visiting delegations.
The Election Commission of India, ECI, has issued orders for placing six officials, including
four policemen, under suspension for alleged lapses at a few polling stations of Agra
Division Teacher's constituency on the 23rd of this month.
month. According to an ECI statement, the suspensions were ordered on the basis of an
inquiry report filed by the Divisional Commissioner, Agra Come Returning Officer for Agra Division
Teacher's constituency.
In our bilingual live phone-in program, Public Speak at 9.30pm tonight, we will bring a
discussion on Public Ravens Portal, Empowering Citizens Through Transparent and Accountable
Governance with Sanjeev Saxena, Senior Technical Director in ICDARPG.
The Indian Olympic Association has announced the contingent for the
2026 Summer Youth Olympic Games set to begin from 31st of this month in Senegal.
A 17-member athlete contingent, including India's promising young table tennis player
Sarthak Arya, will take part in the games across 11 sports.
Benchmark domestic equity indices rose nearly 0.7% today, snapping a four-session losing streak.
